item.title: ‘Sitaram, Sitaram’ from the dugout! Aaryavir Sehwag, Lakshya Raichandani relive the nerve-wracking India-Pakistan U19 Asia Cup final
item.description: NEW DELHI: India's Under-19 Asia Cup triumph over Pakistan was sealed only in the final moments of a gripping contest, but for the youngsters who experienced the pressure first-hand, the memories of that nerve-wracking evening will last much longer. From Aaryavir Sehwag battling a swollen arm to keep his team in the hunt to captain Lakshya Raichandani trying to stay composed amid the tension, the two heroes have offered a glimpse into the emotions that accompanied India's thrilling title-winning chase. In a video shared by the BCCI, Sehwag and Raichandani looked back at the dramatic final in Oman, where India chased down Pakistan's imposing 338-run target with a last-ball boundary from Mohit Ulva. Sehwag revealed how he chose to continue batting despite considerable pain after being struck on the arm, while also recalling how chanting 'Sitaram, Sitaram' from the dugout helped him remain calm as the match headed towards a tense finish. ‘I might not get the chance for India-Pakistan again’ Sehwag, who scored 58 off 61 balls, said his arm had gone numb after being hit and that the swelling was significant. However, the thought of potentially not getting another opportunity to play Pakistan in such a high-profile final pushed him to fight through the pain. "When I got hit on the arm, my arm went numb and it was really paining, it was really paining a lot. And when Suresh sir came, and he saw the swelling, he told me that, you know, it's a lot of swelling. And then I was just thinking that I might not get the chance for India-Pakistan again, and definitely not in the final, the last Under-19 India event, and I could not leave India, my team like this, and I had to fight it out. And I am grateful to God that I got the power and courage to fight through that pain there, and contribute to the team, and it was amazing," Sehwag junior said. The opener's contribution proved crucial as India made a strong start to the chase before Pakistan fought back to put the result in doubt. Sehwag also revealed that he began chanting 'Sitaram, Sitaram' from the 32nd over, drawing comfort from the belief that India could still get over the line. "I had noticed Lakshya also. I don't know which name he was chanting, but I was chanting "Sitaram Sitaram" from the 32nd over. So I was chanting it from the 32nd over, and obviously there was belief in the team, and quite a lot, you know, everyone was sitting in one place, not moving from their place. And everyone had the belief that the boys would do it, the boys would do it. And eventually, by God's grace was there, and (Mohit) Ulva hit that final shot, and everything went in India's favour," said Aaryavir. The tournament turned out to be a memorable one for Sehwag, who was named Player of the Tournament after scoring 361 runs in five matches at an average of 90.25. item.title: Chloe Kitts Tells USC Trojans To Stop Asking Who Is Real SC
item.description: South Carolina Gamecocks forward Chloe Kitts (21) rebounds the ball during the NCAA women’s basketball game Thursday, Nov. 12, 2026 against the Clemson Tigers at Littlejohn Coliseum in Clemson, South Carolina. USA TODAY Network via Reuters Connect South Carolina forward Chloe Kitts told USC Trojans fans to stop asking who the real SC is after her team won 89-85 on Sunday. The Gamecocks defeated the No. 3-ranked Trojans in Greenville, South Carolina, on Nov. 15, 2026. The victory that settled the rivalry score saw Kitts record 15 points and 12 rebounds. She made her comments right before leaving the press conference room following the game. The Battle for the Acronym The Trojans of Southern California and the Gamecocks of South Carolina both claim the USC acronym. The New York Post reported that Sunday’s matchup was billed as the “Battle for the Real SC” among women’s basketball fans. This title set the stage for a high-stakes game between two of the country’s best teams. On Friday, the Trojans overcame a Federal Aviation Administration ground stop for all U.S. airports to arrive at the game on time. Perhaps the last-minute travel changes impacted the Trojans, as they lost to the No. 1-ranked Gamecocks. The final score of 89-85 showed how close the contest remained until the end. JuJu Watkins played for Southern California during the second half of the NCAA college basketball game. A Viral Postgame Moment Kitts gave Trojans fans a harsh reminder about the rivalry during her postgame press conference. Right before leaving the room, she said, “Wait! So, now you can stop asking who the real SC is, because we are.” She then stood up and beckoned for her teammate Tessa Johnson to agree with her. This direct comment has gone viral on social media since the game ended. Social media went viral with a clip of Kitts’ comment, as the @espnW post amassed over 150,000 views in two hours. The New York Post noted that the clip shows Kitts letting fans know after getting the dub over USC. Kitts and the Gamecocks have now definitely taken the bragging rights from JuJu Watkins and the Women of Troy. As two of the nation’s top squads, these teams could very well meet again in the postseason. The New York Post suggested that perhaps the final “Battle for the Real SC” is still to come.

item.title: Fabrizio Romano reveals major Liverpool transfer concern
item.description: Fabrizio Romano reveals major Liverpool transfer concern Liverpool Goalkeeper Situation Growing More Delicate as Alisson and Giorgi Mamardashvili Futures Intersect Liverpool are approaching an important call in the goalkeeping department, with the futures of Alisson Becker and Giorgi Mamardashvili now appearing increasingly linked. Credit to Fabrizio Romano on his YouTube channel, whose latest update pointed to a situation that could soon demand clarity from all parties. The central issue is straightforward. Alisson is into the final year of his Liverpool contract and has publicly indicated a desire to stay. Early discussions over a fresh deal have reportedly begun, which on the surface would look like encouraging news for Liverpool given his standing as one of the elite goalkeepers in world football. Yet that is only one side of the story. Mamardashvili, signed with a clear eye on Liverpool’s long-term planning, is at a stage of his career where patience has limits. At 26, he is no longer a developing prospect content to wait indefinitely. He wants to play, and Liverpool know that. Alisson Contract Talks Raise Bigger Questions Romano explained the balance of power around Alisson has shifted and said: “Liverpool are no longer masters of Alisson’s destiny, let’s put it that way. Last summer they were able to say, ‘Stay with us, we’ll extend for another year, we’ll activate the option.’ Now that option has expired, so Alisson can decide his future. “There is certainly a possibility that Alisson will remain at Liverpool. However, the situation involving him and Giorgi Mamardashvili is becoming increasingly complicated. “This is because Mamardashvili is not a player who wants to remain a backup goalkeeper indefinitely. He is playing second fiddle while waiting for the door to open for a starting spot at Liverpool and at some point, a decision will have to be made.” https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=u2VBzDZiPcs That assessment tallies with wider reporting around the issue. If Alisson commits to a new contract and remains first choice, Liverpool will almost certainly need to address Mamardashvili’s pathway immediately, whether through assurances, a revised plan, or a market decision. Giorgi Mamardashvili Patience Nearing Its Limit There is little mystery over why the Georgia international may be unsettled by the current landscape. Goalkeepers often have to wait longer than outfield players for their opening, but they also need regular minutes to sustain momentum, rhythm and reputation. Mamardashvili has shown enough in cup appearances to suggest he is capable of much more than sporadic involvement. That leaves Liverpool balancing present quality with future succession. Alisson remains the established number one and, on merit, there is no obvious case to dislodge him. Mamardashvili, though, represents a serious asset whose value lies in playing, not standing still. item.description: Everton are in the race to sign Brazilian wonderkid Everton and Brighton Tracking Vitao as Atletico Mineiro Fight to Protect €20m Release Clause Everton are among the clubs showing interest in Atletico Mineiro centre-back Vitao, with TeamTalk reporting that the 18-year-old is attracting growing Premier League attention ahead of January. Brighton are also firmly in the picture, and at this stage their move appears to be the most advanced. The Brazilian side are understood to be “working extremely hard to secure their 18-year-old centre-back Vitao on a new contract and raise his release clause”, a clear sign of how highly they rate the teenager. Vitao is under contract until December 2028 and currently has a “€20million (£16.7m) release clause applicable to foreign clubs”. That clause is central to the situation. Atletico Mineiro hold 80 per cent of his economic rights, with the remainder split between the player and his representatives, and they want stronger protection before interest turns into bids. According to the original report from TeamTalk, the club want improved terms, a salary rise and a bigger release clause to strengthen their position. Vitao transfer battle gathering pace There is a firm line from Mineiro for now. “Any offer falling below the existing clause will be resisted as much as possible in January,” while there are also “suggestions from sources that the club has set a minimum figure of €18m (£15m) before they would be prepared to enter serious discussions in January”. Their preference is to keep Vitao until the summer, giving him more regular football in Brazil and potentially increasing his market value further. Photo: IMAGO Even so, the direction of travel feels obvious. “Momentum is building towards a possible January move,” and that will alert clubs who specialise in identifying emerging talent before the market becomes crowded or the price climbs again. Everton are also in the mix, with several major European clubs watching developments, including Real Madrid, Barcelona, Paris Saint-Germain and AC Milan. Vitao has already made around 18 senior appearances this season and scored once, establishing himself under Eduardo Dominguez. He is described as a defender with physicality, aerial strength and technical composure, qualities that tend to translate well to the Premier League. item.title: Dan Orlovsky speaks on the ‘good learning moments’ from Fernando Mendoza’s NFL debut
item.description: Photo by Mitchell Leff/Getty Images Fernando Mendoza impressed a few people with his NFL debut, and former quarterback Dan Orlovsky was one of them. The first overall pick of the 2026 NFL Draft scored a touchdown on his first drive, as he rushed through the Seattle Seahawks defence to help the Las Vegas Raiders take the lead. After a decent first half, the Raiders were not able to do much in the second half, as the Seahawks’ defence showed why they are one of the most elite units in the NFL. Dan Orlovsky reveals learning moments from Fernando Mendoza’s debut Mendoza was sacked six times during the game. Four of them came in the second half, as he got a taste of what NFL defences are like. Having seen the first overall pick in action, Orlovsky spoke about what the player could learn from his first start as an NFL QB. “I was impressed with Fernando Mendoza and I thought he did some really good things, got through some progressions. I think the big learning thing for Fernando is you better know when your unblocked guys come in and you’re hot, and then two, the play declined after pockets got a little muddy for him and again, that’s going to be a learning moment for him,” said Orlovsky on The Pat McAfee Show. After his first start, Mendoza was extremely positive and took a lot from the game against the Seahawks. “A lot of credit to them and coach Macdonald…It’s good to get punched in the face because now, it’s a great opportunity to grow and learn and to really unveil all the deficiencies that I have in my game and as a future leader, future hopeful leader of this offence,” said Mendoza in his press conference. The Raiders will next be taking on the Denver Broncos, another team with a good defensive unit. Having learnt the lessons from his debut, Mendoza will be hoping to put on a good show and help the Raiders secure a win against their division rivals. The Spain international has scored seven goals and grabbed five assists in 11 appearances for Barcelona this season across all competitions. The 23-year-old is currently one of the most talented playmakers in La Liga. Hence, it is no wonder that the Blues are showing interest in recruiting him next year. item.description: Oklahoma tight ends coach Jason Witten, left, talks with coach Brent Venables during a Sooners football spring practice in Norman, Okla., Thursday, April 9, 2026. Credit: USA TODAY Network via Reuters Connect (Reuters) The Oklahoma Sooners are rolling. Now 2-0 since firing offensive coordinator Ben Arbuckle and naming TE coach Jason Witten as interim OC, the Sooners pick up another big win against Ole Miss. Oklahoma spoils Ole Miss’s CFP aspirations, beating the Rebels 24-17. After the game was moved to Sunday because Ole Miss did not make the trip on Friday night, Oklahoma set the tone early. The game started with a long touchdown drive, 13 plays, and over 7 minutes taken off the clock. Ole Miss had to punt on the next drive, and Sooners’ WR1 Isaiah Sategna III returned the punt for a touchdown, sprinting down the right side of the field, with help from a major block by WR Manny Choice. Witten’s biggest change to the offense is that he’s playing to the roster’s strengths. He’s not trying to make this offense something it’s not meant to be. A huge part of that is committing to the run and not putting too much on QB John Mateer’s plate. Oklahoma isn’t living and dying on the pass game like they were, which limits opportunities for Mateer to make a mistake and throw an interception. Mateer’s usage in the run game has significantly increased, which should’ve happened at the start of the season. In 2025, Mateer led the team in rushing yards and scored 8 rushing touchdowns. Against Ole Miss on Sunday, Mateer led the team in rushing with 70 yards. In addition to the rushing yards, Mateer scored his first rushing touchdown of the season. After the game, SoonerScoop’s George Stoia asked Witten if he wanted to be Oklahoma’s offensive coordinator. Witten responded with enthusiasm and said, “Absolutely.” Witten is trending in that direction, but still has work to do. item.title: Rams Crush Cardinals 34-6 As Stafford Proves Depth Without Stars
item.description: Matt Kartozian-Imagn Images On Sunday at State Farm Stadium, the Arizona Cardinals were thoroughly beaten 34-6 by the Los Angeles Rams, claiming their fourth consecutive victory. Matthew Stafford threw three touchdown passes while Aaron Donald finally broke a 1,050-day sack drought. This victory proves the team can win big even when their best players sit on the sidelines due to injury. Sean McVay finally abandoned his predictable offensive tendencies to get creative with his playbook. For the first time, Kyren Williams and Blake Corum ran together in the backfield as he deployed several different personnel groupings. Stafford passed to nine distinct receivers, demonstrating trust in his inexperienced targets while the stars were absent. McVay Finds Answers Without Top Weapons Four weeks after an embarrassing loss at SoFi Stadium, the Rams coach found the right answers to beat a former assistant. Puka Nacua and Davante Adams were sidelined, yet the offense moved the ball with ease. Xavier Smith, Tyler Higbee, and Davis Allen all caught touchdown passes in a diverse attack that confused the defense. The New York Post reported that McVay went digging through his playbook like a grandma searching for candy. He found something sweet by using jumbo packages with extra linemen. Following their initial encounter where the Cardinals anticipated his every move, this strategy left Arizona defensive coordinator Mike LaFleur puzzled. Injury Woes Mount For Los Angeles The injury report for Los Angeles now resembles a casualty list as starters keep going down. The early departure of starting center Coleman Shelton forced backup Dylan McMahon into the game, only for McMahon to also suffer an injury. Bill Murray entered the lineup at left guard after Beaux Limmer moved to center, as the team faces difficulties maintaining cohesion. Significant injuries have already claimed Adams, Nacua, cornerback Jaylen Watson, and defensive tackle Poona Ford for Los Angeles. The team cannot afford to lose any more players if they want to keep their winning streak alive. The offensive line got dismantled during the game, yet the team still found a way to dominate. Donald Breaks The Sack Drought Aaron Donald ended a drought that stretched nearly three years with a sack on Cardinals rookie quarterback Carson Beck. Early in the second quarter, Myles Garrett pressured Beck into stepping up in the pocket where Donald was waiting to pounce. It was Donald’s first sack since December 31, 2023, a span of 1,050 days. The Rams defense finished with five sacks and two forced fumbles to slam the door on Arizona. Donald later added another half-sack to help secure the blowout victory. The Rams improved to 6-4 on the season with this convincing performance against their division rival.

item.title: Caprile on Cagliari chance, Conte anger and Albania opportunity
item.description: Caprile on Cagliari chance, Conte anger and Albania opportunity Elia Caprile has been the most effective goalkeeper in Serie A this season at Cagliari, but reveals Antonio Conte ‘did not take it well’ when he left Napoli, is open to playing for Albania, and nearly gave up his career. The 25-year-old has kept four clean sheets in 11 Serie A games so far this season, more than any other goalkeeper in the division, and also made more saves than anyone else. Despite that, he knows that he’s very far behind in the ranking for Italy, where Gianluigi Donnarumma, Guglielmo Vicario, Marco Carnesecchi and Alex Meret are all ahead of him. Caprile flourishing at Cagliari CAGLIARI, ITALY – JANUARY 17: Elia Caprile of Cagliari looks on during the Serie A match between Cagliari Calcio and Juventus FC at Stadio Sant’Elia on January 17, 2026 in Cagliari, Italy. (Photo by Enrico Locci/Getty Images) “I would love to silence all those who wouldn’t bet a cent on me when I was little, that fire inside me is still burning,” Caprile told the Corriere della Sera newspaper. “I thought of quitting so many times, especially when a few coaches were mean to me. I wasn’t playing, I was shorter than the other kids, I was fat. “I was made to feel bad about it and lost my way, but I got advice from two goalkeeping coaches Bressan and Squizzi at the moment I needed them the most. They showed me football is made of sacrifice, both before and after training.” UDINE, ITALY – OCTOBER 05: Elia Caprile of Cagliari makes a save during the Serie A match between Udinese Calcio and Cagliari Calcio at Stadio Friuli on October 05, 2025 in Udine, Italy. (Photo by Timothy Rogers/Getty Images) Caprile has never played for Italy at senior level, and now has Albanian citizenship thanks to his partner. “I don’t know if something can come from it, so far no Federation has knocked at my door. If they do, then I will evaluate.” He already made the decision to walk away from Napoli in 2025 when frustrated at the lack of playing time, and took the opportunity to shine at Cagliari. UDINE, ITALY – OCTOBER 05: Arthur Atta of Udinese heads the ball on to the crossbar as Elia Caprile of Cagliari attempts a save during the Serie A match between Udinese Calcio and Cagliari Calcio at Stadio Friuli on October 05, 2025 in Udine, Italy. (Photo by Timothy Rogers/Getty Images) “Conte told me to stay and fight for my place with Meret, so he was honest, and so was I. He chose Alex and won the Scudetto, so it was wise, but I was 23 and really wanted to play. I felt the physical need to be on the pitch,” explained Caprile. “So in January, I told him I wanted to leave. Conte did not take it well, but he understood.”

item.title: Matt LaFleur makes his case for retaining Luke Butkus as Packers offensive line coach
item.description: GREEN BAY – A day after his offensive line was equally outcoached and outplayed, Green Bay Packers coach Matt LaFleur agreed all aspects need to be better. Where he broke from popular sentiment is who should be leading that effort. LaFleur made clear he will be making no change to his offensive line coach. Luke Butkus , who began working on LaFleur’s staff as an assistant offensive line coach in 2019 and is in his fifth season as the unit’s position coach, will remain in his role. “He was the same guy when we were rolling,” LaFleur said. “I think it’s easy to pinpoint and point the finger, and everybody wants to pinpoint blame, but the blame can go to everybody. So it’s all of us in this together. Certainly it starts with myself, and then it goes to everybody else, and it’s coaches and players collectively.” It’s true the Packers offensive line has never struggled under Butkus like it has this season. On Butkus’ biography on the Packers website, the team notes this offensive line was the only unit in the NFL to rank among the top 10 in fewest sacks allowed each of the past four seasons. The Packers are unlikely to extend that streak this season. Their offensive line has allowed quarterback Jordan Love to be sacked 25 times this season, tied for the 13th most in the league. Eight sacks came in their loss to the Minnesota Vikings , the most they’ve allowed in a game in more than a decade. The eight sacks were part of 12 quarterback hits. In two games against the Vikings this season, the Packers have allowed 27 quarterback hits, including a dozen sacks. “It was pretty bad,” LaFleur said of the film review from his offensive line’s latest meltdown. “It wasn’t good enough. Certainly some things that schematically we didn’t do a good job with, and then ultimately there were some execution things as well.” The Vikings have the NFL’s best pass rush. They’ve routinely left offensive lines in ruin this season with defensive coordinator Brian Flores’ aggressive blitz scheme, but their eight sacks were a high in any game this season. It inflated the Packers’ season totals, considering almost half of their sacks allowed have come in two games against the Vikings, but their latest demolition was also a new low point. It isn’t ideal to have a new low point 10 games into a season. “Bottom line,” LaFleur said, “is they’ve given everybody problems that they’ve gone against. I think, quite honestly, we did the best job against them Week 1, and we still were talking about how many times our quarterback got hit. item.description: If blowing a 17-point lead and losing a game pivotal to their playoff hopes wasn't bad enough for the Texans on Sunday in Cleveland, the loss came at the hands of their erstwhile franchise QB Deshaun Watson. (Brett Coomer/Houston Chronicle) As one watched the Houston Texans collapse Sunday and take a devastating loss to the Cleveland Browns on the shores of Lake Erie, it was easy to declare it ranks among the worst defeats in the franchise's 25-season history. A colleague was quick to note, "Such a big menu, too." Indeed, like a trip to the Cheesecake Factory. But we're going to drill down on the specials, or in this case, losses with blown leads of 17 points or more, of which the Texans now have eight after coughing up a 17-0 advantage in Cleveland. Without further ado, here's a ranking of the worst blown leads and subsequent losses in Texans history. 1. 2019 playoffs: Chiefs 51, Texans 31 We might never see a Texans loss worse than this one in the AFC divisional round at Kansas City. They were up 24-0 in the second quarter with about 40 minutes separating the Texans from their first AFC championship game, which would've been at home against the Titans. aka the team that ditched Houston. Hollywood writers couldn't cook up such a scenario. But the Texans somehow lost that lead before halftime. Everything that could go wrong did go wrong: A 58-yard kickoff return allowed, Bill O'Brien's disastrous fake-punt call at his own 31 with a 24-7 lead, a fumbled kickoff return … we'll spare you any more pain. Incredibly, the Texans became the first team to lead a playoff game by 20 or more points - and lose by 20 points. Even more incredibly, O'Brien got a promotion with general manager added to his title after the collapse. 2. 2013 Week 4: Seahawks 23, Texans 20 Arguably the game that changed the course of Texans history . They were 2-1 and hosting the 3-0 Seahawks. Houston led 20-3 at halftime and was up 20-13 with less than three minutes left and had third-and-4 from the Seattle 40. But Matt Schaub's ill-advised throw under pressure was intercepted by Richard Sherman, who returned it 58 yards for the tying touchdown - while losing his shoe. But a Browns pass interference penalty helped gift Houston the go-ahead touchdown and a lead in the final minutes. And the Texans couldn't hold on and their playoff hopes took a gut punch. item.title: Penguins Legend Jaromir Jagr All But Announces Retirement
item.description: Pittsburgh Penguins Legend Jaromir Jagr Makes Major Career Announcement Getty PITTSBURGH, PENNSYLVANIA - FEBRUARY 18: Jaromir Jagr waves to the crowd after he skated in warmups following his jersey retirement ceremony before the game between the Pittsburgh Penguins and the Los Angeles Kings at PPG PAINTS Arena on February 18, 2024 in Pittsburgh, Pennsylvania. (Photo by Justin Berl/Getty Images) Getty The Pittsburgh Penguins have a couple of players who would qualify as a legend. Mario Lemieux, Jaromir Jagr, and current captain Sidney Crosby are probably the three best examples of such a label. Two of these players are still playing in Jagr and Crosby. However, it sounds like that is changing for one of them. In a surprising turn of events, it appears that the ageless wonder, Jagr, 54 is ready to be done playing hockey. In a new interview with iSport, he all but confirms his upcoming retirement. “If you have nothing more to give and you feel like you’re doing more harm than good, it’s time to leave. But I think I’ve squeezed every last drop out of it,” Jagr reveals in the exclusive interview. “I believe that the body is a brilliant tool. If I really wanted to, it would give me meaning, or I had the motivation, then I could do it. But it doesn’t make sense to me anymore.” “If it doesn’t even give you joy anymore and you do something just out of obligation, it’s not worth it. Life is too short to do things you have to. If you have the opportunity, do only what you want. What you see meaning in. That’s freedom… Otherwise, I think that we don’t have much freedom left in the world.” “I was the luckiest that my work was both a hobby and a joy.” Jagr hasn’t played in the NHL for many years. He finished his NHL career with 1921 points in 1733 games, the second-most career points in NHL history. Jaromir Jagr’s Next Stop: the Hockey Hall of Fame Getty PITTSBURGH, PENNSYLVANIA – FEBRUARY 18: Jaromir Jagr waves to the crowd after he skated in warmups following his jersey retirement ceremony before the game between the Pittsburgh Penguins and the Los Angeles Kings at PPG PAINTS Arena on February 18, 2024 in Pittsburgh, Pennsylvania. (Photo by Justin Berl/Getty Images) Some fans wonder if Jagr is already in the Hockey Hall of Fame. The short answer is no. For a player to be considered for the Hockey Hall of Fame, they need to be three years removed from their last season of playing hockey. With the end of Jagr’s playing days seemingly upon us, three years from now expect to see Jagr’s name show up on the ballot. And then expect him to get in right away. Jagr has won multiple Stanley Cups, individual awards, and he’s the second all-time leading point scorer ever in the NHL. That is very much the definition of a Hall of Fame career. item.title: 'It's growing': Jude Bellingham underwear ad shows soccer's US appeal
item.description: Bellingham helped steer England to a famous 6-4 victory over France in the third place play-off with an inspired 98th minute solo spectacular (ROBERTO SCHMIDT) Soccer star Jude Bellingham has a trophy case of accolades to his name. But the England and Real Madrid attacking midfielder has been elevated to the pantheon of US pop culture immortality with his own extra-large Calvin Klein underwear billboard in Manhattan. Measuring 75 feet by 55 feet (22.9 by 16.8 meters), the giant billboard overlooking one of the Big Apple's busiest shopping havens has drawn crowds of admirers. It also highlights the outsize cultural impact the soccer World Cup had on the US, which cohosted the tournament with Mexico and Canada. Bellingham is pictured holding his signature arms-stretched celebratory pose and sporting only a pair of white Calvin Klein hip briefs for modesty. "We were just in the area, and then my little sister, she was like, 'I got to see the Jude Bellingham poster' -- especially after they beat Mexico in the World Cup, right?" said store manager George Lozano, 30, whose sister Jackie, 24, snapped a photo on her phone. "I personally wouldn't think (most Americans) would recognize him. I think it's still growing. It's growing in terms of the US... support for soccer. But I think now this would definitely help, right?" Bellingham became a breakout social media sensation during the summer World Cup for his youthful good looks and prowess on the pitch. Bellingham's selection for Calvin Klein's landmark SoHo billboard puts him alongside cultural titans including Bad Bunny, Jeremy Allen White and Justin Bieber, who bared nearly all before him. "I like him but he's not my favorite," said French tourist Roxane Marin, 33, of Bellingham, who helped steer England to a famous 6-4 victory over France in the third-place playoff with an inspired 98th-minute solo spectacular. "I watch football, but I can't remember if I saw that match," she added to AFP after taking a close-up of the billboard. Marin insisted she had happened upon the billboard by chance, "but I think there are people who come on purpose." gw/pnb
